description: ClassBridge Domain Adaptation Layer Glossary - Curated standard technical translations for Indic languages to prevent MT hallucination or mistranslation.

eigenvalue.definition: A scalar associated with a linear system of equations that measures factor expansion along an eigenvector.

eigenvector.definition: A non-zero vector whose direction remains unchanged when a linear transformation is applied.

gradient descent.definition: First-order iterative optimization algorithm for finding a local minimum of a differentiable function.

backpropagation.definition: Algorithm used to calculate gradients of loss function with respect to weights using chain rule.

neural network.definition: A computational model inspired by biological nervous systems consisting of interconnected nodes/layers.

loss function.definition: Function that maps an event or values of one or more variables onto a real number representing cost.

learning rate.definition: Tuning parameter in an optimization algorithm that determines the step size at each iteration.

overfitting.definition: Modeling error where function corresponds too closely or exactly to a particular set of data.

underfitting.definition: When a mathematical model cannot adequately capture the underlying structure of the data.

activation function.definition: Node function that defines output given an input or set of inputs, introducing non-linearity.

photosynthesis.definition: Process by which phototrophs convert light energy into chemical energy (glucose).

mitochondria.definition: Double-membrane-bound cellular organelle that produces adenosine triphosphate (ATP).

cellular respiration.definition: Metabolic reactions converting biochemical energy from nutrients into ATP.

ribosome.definition: Macromolecular machine that performs biological protein synthesis.

thermodynamics.definition: Branch of physics dealing with heat, work, temperature, and statistical relation to energy.

entropy.definition: Scientific concept associated with state of disorder, randomness, or uncertainty.

momentum.definition: The quantity of motion of a moving body, measured as a product of its mass and velocity.

kinetic energy.definition: The energy an object possesses by reason of its motion, equal to 1/2 m v^2.

potential energy.definition: Stored energy held by an object because of its relative position, stress, or electric charge.

capacitance.definition: The ratio of the change in an electric charge in a system to the corresponding change in its electric potential.

inductance.definition: Property of an electrical conductor by which a change in current flowing through it induces an electromotive force.

matrix multiplication.definition: Binary operation that produces a matrix from two matrices with compatible inner dimensions.

determinant.definition: Scalar value computed from elements of a square matrix encoding transformation properties.

derivative.definition: The rate of change of a function with respect to an independent variable.

integral.definition: Mathematical object assigning numbers to functions representing area, volume, displacement.

polynomial.definition: Mathematical expression consisting of indeterminates and coefficients involving only addition, subtraction, multiplication.

vector space.definition: Set of objects (vectors) that may be added together and multiplied by scalars.

asymptotic notation.definition: Mathematical notations (Big-O, Omega, Theta) describing limiting behavior of execution complexity.

time complexity.definition: Computational complexity that describes the amount of computer time taken to run an algorithm.

space complexity.definition: Memory space required by an algorithm to execute as a function of the length of input.

binary search.definition: Search algorithm that finds position of a target value within a sorted array in O(log n) time.

recursion.definition: Method of solving a problem where the solution depends on solutions to smaller instances of the same problem.

dynamic programming.definition: Algorithmic technique solving complex problems by breaking them down into overlapping subproblems.

graph traversal.definition: Problem of visiting each vertex in a graph (BFS or DFS).

hash table.definition: Data structure implementing an associative array, mapping keys to values using a hash function.

catalyst.definition: Substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without undergoing permanent chemical change.

covalent bond.definition: Chemical bond involving sharing of electron pairs between atoms.

exothermic.definition: Chemical reaction accompanied by release of heat (negative delta H).

endothermic.definition: Chemical reaction accompanied by absorption of heat (positive delta H).

activation energy.definition: Minimum energy required for a chemical reaction to occur.

equilibrium.definition: State where forward reaction rate equals reverse reaction rate.

oxidation.definition: Process involving loss of electrons or increase in oxidation state.

reduction.definition: Process involving gain of electrons or decrease in oxidation state.

differential equation.definition: Mathematical equation that relates one or more functions and their derivatives.

partial derivative.definition: Derivative of a function of several variables with respect to one variable, holding others constant.

transformer.definition: Deep learning model architecture utilizing self-attention mechanisms widely used in NLP.

attention mechanism.definition: Technique allowing neural networks to dynamically focus on specific parts of input sequence.

convolution.definition: Mathematical operation on two functions expressing how the shape of one is modified by the other.

cross-entropy.definition: Measure of difference between two probability distributions over the same set of events.

stochastic gradient descent.definition: Iterative optimization technique that calculates gradient on random mini-batches rather than whole dataset.
